newsitem.title: UK: Iron supplements linked to improved learning.
newsitem.headline: Iron supplements linked to improved learning.

text.p: American doctors said on Friday iron pills given to teenage girls with mild iron deficiency, a common nutritional disorder, can help their learning.

Ann Bruner and co-workers at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine in Baltimore, Maryland tested 78 teenage girls who had low iron levels, but were not anaemic, for attention and memory to measure cognitive functioning.
During an eight-week study half the group were given iron supplements and half received placebos. They were then tested again.

"Regression analysis showed that girls who received iron performed better on a test for verbal learning and memory than girls in the control group," Bruner said in a report in the Lancet medical journal.
Iron deficiency affects about 20 percent of the world population. It is particularly bad in developing countries but even in the United States up to 25 percent of adolescent girls are iron deficient.
"This study suggests that, even in the absence of anaemia, iron supplementation improves verbal learning and memory among adolescent girls," said Bruner.
Further studies of the effects of the condition are needed, she added.
